title.title: Fourier series converge almost everywhere in $L\log L$
title.subtitle: Claim: for every $f$ with $\int |f|\log(2+|f|) < \infty$, the partial sums $S_N f \to f$ almost everywhere

plain: Rebuild a jagged signal from pure tones: for which signals does the rebuilding settle almost everywhere?

beats.text: Each ring: a space where Fourier series converge almost everywhere
Kolmogorov: in $L^1$ they can diverge. The known rings crept toward it
The claim: the natural boundary, $L\log L$, is a convergence space too

steps: Reduce the sums to one estimate on a tree of dyadic intervals
Treat each frequency guess as a noisy observation of the input
An entropy budget caps the total cost, so the sums converge

achievement.label: The L log L conjecture, recorded by Lie
statement: f \in L\log L(\mathbb T) \;\Longrightarrow\; S_N f(x) \to f(x) \text{ for a.e. } x
achievement.note: No Lean; 76 pages of an entropy method far from time-frequency analysis

voice.text: Square-integrable signals converge; merely integrable ones can fail. Where is the line?
Reduce to a dyadic tree, then cap the total cost with an entropy budget.
Claimed: L log L signals converge almost everywhere.
